historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case forward 5-year average (17/12/9/7/6). Historical anchors are unusable as a forward proxy: the 3-yr revenue CAGR (2.9%) spans the FY2023 dine-out-recovery slump (-15%) then +6%/+21%; equity CAGR is distorted by the Nov-2023 IPO proceeds and FY2024-25 buybacks and dividends; owner-FCF CAGR (39%) is off a depressed FY2022 base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 5.4% diverges >30% from EPS 3-yr CAGR 22.8% and revenue 2.9%: equity growth is suppressed by RMB531m of dividends and RMB257m of buybacks in FY2024-25, EPS is flattered by the share count falling 7% and the FY2024 Dmall fair-value loss base. None of the three is a clean forward anchor; the forward path is judged from store-count guidance and margin run-rate instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series: FY2022 139.7 (167.3 - 4.6 SBC - 23.0 interest), FY2023 511.5 (543.3 - 0 - 31.8), FY2024 368.1 (407.0 - 0 - 38.9), FY2025 376.2 (392.5 - 0 - 16.2). Only four full fiscal years are available (FY2022-FY2025), so 5-year CAGRs are null. Owner-FCF CAGR (39.1%) exceeds reported (32.9%) because interest income fell with the cash pile -- SBC is not a factor here.

scenario_narratives.base: Store network reaches ~13,100 by end-FY2026 and keeps adding at a fading pace as township penetration matures; store efficiency grows high-single-digit on the large-format upgrade and Douyin-to-store traffic. Gross margin stays under pressure from copycat chains and supermarket store-in-store formats, but selling and admin leverage holds operating EBITDA margin flat at ~8.5%. The Danzhou factory buildout keeps FY2026 capex at ~3.8% of revenue before it normalises. Working capital gives no tailwind: rising franchisee receivables and prepayments are assumed to absorb what supplier credit would otherwise release. Dividends and buybacks continue to be funded partly from the RMB1.4bn cash pile.
scenario_narratives.bull: Category consolidation favours the scale leader: regional copycats exit, store adds re-accelerate toward the original >14,500 trajectory, and the four-store-format strategy plus Guoquan Farm premium lines lift store efficiency double-digit. Vertical integration (one-product-one-factory, Danzhou base) and AI supply-chain scheduling recover ~1pp of EBITDA margin to 9.5% by FY2030. Negative net working capital turns back into a modest cash source (5% of revenue growth) as payables scale with volume. The 70% de-rating reverses toward the CMBI/CICC/Huatai target range.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2023-style dine-out recovery or further consumption downgrade stalls same-store sales while supermarket store-in-store formats undercut franchisee economics; store closures rise above the <4% guided rate and net adds stop after FY2026, so revenue falls 5% and 3% in FY2027-28 before stabilising near flat. Gross margin slides below 21% and operating EBITDA margin settles at 6.8%. The H1 FY2026 receivables/prepayments build proves to be franchisee support rather than seasonality, and capex on the new plant is largely stranded. The terminal multiple is capped at 12x for a no-growth wholesaler. The business remains solvent throughout -- net cash covers all debt several times over -- so this is a value-destruction case, not a going-concern case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Guoquan is valued as what it is: a thin-margin wholesale distributor whose growth is the franchise store count, not a franchisor with royalty economics. The house case gives it no margin re-expansion, no working-capital tailwind, a flat share count despite ongoing buybacks, and a 15x terminal cap, and still arrives well above the price because roughly half the market capitalisation is net cash and investment assets on the balance sheet. The valuation question is therefore less about the DCF mechanics than about whether the market is right to apply a deep China-small-cap discount to the cash and to the durability of the franchise network -- which is why the bear weight is doubled rather than the WACC inflated.
key_risks_to_valuation: Franchise store economics: a rise in closures above the <4% guided rate would turn store growth negative and the base case into the bear case; the company does not disclose per-store P&L.

Earnings quality: H1 FY2026 OCF of -RMB102m against +RMB213m net income; if receivables and prepayments to franchisees are channel support rather than seasonality, reported profit overstates cash earnings.
Low-barrier competition and gross-margin slide (22.8% -> 21.5% in two years) with no franchise-fee cushion.
Capital allocation: FY2025 dividends + buybacks (RMB572m) exceeded owner FCF; the cash pile the valuation leans on is being distributed while borrowings rose to RMB333m.
Cash-pile discount: ~RMB1.6bn of net cash and investments (RMB0.64/share, HK$0.75) is taken at face value; a China-domiciled H-share may never be credited for it in the market.
FX: CNY flows against an HKD quote; a weaker yuan lowers every HKD value proportionally (fx_rate 1.1724 as of 2026-10-16).

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,747,360,400 shares in issue less 176,101,200 treasury shares and repurchased shares pending cancellation = 2,538,284,400 at 17 Aug 2026 (interim-dividend record basis, H1 FY2026 interim report). No dilutive potential ordinary shares in issue (interim note on EPS). Held FLAT: SBC is zero so there is nothing to expense; ongoing buybacks (RMB167.9m in H1 FY2026) are genuine accretion the model does not credit, which is conservative.
inputs.cash_composition: Cash and bank balances 1,151.614 + current FVTPL bank wealth-management products 204.236 + long-term bank deposits 78.954 (all 30 Jun 2026). Restricted cash 112.525 EXCLUDED. Non-current FVTPL unlisted fund 36.0, associates 330.608 and FVOCI equity investments 152.088 are carried in equity_bridge, not cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement and note 7: no share-based payment expense in FY2023-FY2025 (FY2022: RMB4.6m). SBC-zero market convention; rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow RMB183.9m (116.95m shares); H1 FY2026 a further RMB167.9m. FY2025 dividends RMB388.1m. Distributions + buybacks (RMB572m) exceeded owner FCF (RMB376m) in FY2025, funded from the cash pile.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16 close). Parity check via USD legs: USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6862 = 1.1738, a 0.1% tie confirming rate and direction. No dual listing exists. All flows and per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD to match current_price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, equity risk premium ~7.0% for a China-domiciled consumer franchise supplier, beta ~1.2 (HK-listed China small/mid-cap consumer, low-barrier category) = ~10.2% cost of equity, plus ~0.3pp for a thin-float H-share with a 70% drawdown and lock-up overhang. Debt is <3% of EV at ~3% coupons and is ignored in the blend. 10.5% is applied identically to all three scenarios; cyclicality, competition and earnings-quality risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal RMB31.2m + lease interest RMB3.1m = RMB34.3m, 0.44% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (RMB69.8m at 30 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from total_debt, which is interest-bearing bank and other borrowings only (256.050 current + 76.664 non-current). da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (PP&E depreciation + intangible amortisation: FY2025 69.1m = 0.88% of revenue; H1 FY2026 42.9m = 1.09%), so EBIT for cash tax is not charged the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Minority interests folded into the cash_tax_rate_path as leakage (attributable-only flows): FY2025 income tax RMB146.8m (24.4% of PBT) + NCI profit share RMB21.0m (3.5%) on an operating EBIT of ~RMB576m gives ~28%; H1 FY2026 NCI fell to RMB1.9m, so 27% is used. No NCI deduction in the bridge (RMB137.6m NCI equity NOT subtracted) -- charging once. Calibration: FY2025 component NOPAT 575 x 0.73 = ~420m vs reported attributable net income 432.9m, the gap being the stripped non-operating income (interest, FV gains, associates) taxed at 25%.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Operating EBITDA post-IFRS-16, excluding interest income, realised/unrealised FVTPL gains, share of associates, FVOCI dividends, FX and disposal items, but INCLUDING recurring government grants (FY2025 RMB59.2m, FY2024 48.3m). FY2025: PBT 600.65 + finance costs 5.78 - interest 16.24 - FV gains 6.06 - associates 9.23 - dividends 0.75 + FX 2.45 + other 0.2 = EBIT ~576.5; + D&A 102.3 = ~678.8m = 8.7% of revenue (the CSV's 708.7 is PBT + finance costs + D&A with nothing stripped). H1 FY2026 8.6% (8.9% ex RMB11.8m litigation one-off) vs H1 FY2025 9.1%; FY2024 6.9%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), with the non-US adaptations (CNY WACC, HKD quote via fx_rate, lease treatment B, NCI as leakage, excluded-income assets in the bridge, SBC-zero). Guoquan is an operating company -- a wholesale supplier to ~12,200 franchised at-home hotpot stores with no franchise fees -- so the routing table sends it to owner-FCF, not to a non-FCF model. The negative H1 FY2026 OCF (-102.4m) is seasonal plus working-capital unwind, not a structural break: H1 FY2025 was also negative (-29.0m) and FY2025 full-year OCF was +588.4m on net income of 453.9m; the H1 pattern is a RMB362m trade-payables unwind after the winter hotpot peak. FY0 is FY2025 (Dec year-end), the last full year; the component build is anchored on FY2025 actuals and H1 FY2026 run-rate, and FY2026 is the guidance year (>13,100 stores, 'stable' core operating profit growth, cut from the March target of >14,500 stores and profit growth 'significantly higher than revenue'). Owner FCF FY2025 = 392.484 reported - 0 SBC - 16.241 interest income = 376.243; the lease charge (34.3m) is applied inside the projection, not in last_fcf. Component-built FY2025 owner FCF is ~RMB293m (3.8% margin) vs the reported-basis 342m after leases, the gap being a +32m working-capital inflow and cash tax paid below the accrued charge -- the forward build uses the more conservative component margin. Capex is elevated by the Danzhou (Hainan) production-base buildout (H1 FY2026 PP&E + land RMB189.5m vs 61.8m prior-year H1) and is normalised from 3.8% of revenue in FY2026 to 1.5% by FY2032. Working-capital capture is 0% in base: net working capital is roughly neutral (inventory + receivables + prepayments 1,624m vs payables + accruals 1,719m at FY2025), but receivables and prepayments to franchisees are the earnings-quality flag, so growth is given no cash tailwind. Terminal cap 15x (12x bear) per the method's rule for structurally slower, low-barrier categories. Price is a regular HKEX close, not after-hours.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~17%: H1 +21.8% actual, H2 decelerating to ~14% as the comparable base (H2 FY2025 revenue 4,570m) toughens and store adds slow to the cut >13,100 target (+13% stores) plus high-single-digit store efficiency. Store adds then fade as township penetration matures in a low-barrier category; 3% terminal-decade growth is roughly China food-retail nominal growth.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 8.7%, H1 FY2026 8.6% (8.9% ex litigation) vs 9.1% prior H1. Gross margin compression (22.8% -> 21.5% over two years) offsets selling/admin leverage; 'stable' core operating profit growth guidance implies a flat-to-slightly-down margin. Held flat at 8.5% -- no re-expansion assumed.
base.capex_rationale: H1 FY2026 PP&E + land use rights RMB189.5m (4.8% of H1 revenue) on the Danzhou production base; FY2026 ~RMB350m, then normalising toward FY2024's 1.9% and below as the factory footprint (7 plants) is complete. Terminal 1.5% vs D&A 1.2% keeps capex above depreciation for a growing network.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the category has demonstrably low entry barriers, revenue fell 15% the last time dine-out recovered (FY2023), the August guidance cut (14,500 -> 13,100 stores, profit growth 'significantly above revenue' -> 'stable') came only five months after it was set, and the receivables/prepayments build behind the negative H1 OCF is an unresolved earnings-quality question. Bull cut to 20% because it requires three independent things to go right -- competitor exit, margin recovery and working capital turning positive -- in a Chinese consumer backdrop management itself describes as 'rational consumption deepening'. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
